en: בִּילוֹן , Bekhoroth VII, 1, see כִּילוֹן

חֲטוֹטֶרֶת, חֲטֶרֶת f. (חטר, compare חוֹטֶר II) (camel’s) hunch, hump. Chullin IX, 2 (Talmud ed. 122ᵃ חטר׳). Shabbat 54ᵃ, see חוֹטֶרֶת.—plural חֲטוֹטָרוֹת, חֲטָרוֹת. Bekhoroth VII, 1 (43ᵃ) בעלי חטוטרות Maimonides (Mishn. sing; Talmud ed. חטרות) hump-backed men; Tosefta ib. V, 2.

יֶתֶר I m. (Biblical Hebrew, see יָתַר)
1) cord, bow-string. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 5 (reference. to Psalms XI, 2), see מִתְחָא
.—2) = יוֹתֵר addition, (adverb) more. Bekhoroth VII, 1 (43ᵃ) וי עליהן וכ׳ Bavli ed. (Mishnah יותר עליהן באדם וכ׳) to these must be added, with reference to blemishes of human beings, the wedge-shaped head &c. Eruvin 83ᵇ י׳על כן more than that. Gittin III, 1 י׳מכן nay, even more; and from
כִּילוֹן, (בִּילוֹן) m. (see אוּבְלָא II) one whose head has the shape of a basket (calathus), wedge-shaped. Bekhoroth VII, 1, explained ib. 43ᵇ. [Mus. refers to Lat. cilo.]
לִפְתָּם, לִפְתָּן I m. (see לֶפֶת), one whose head is turnip-shaped. Bekhoroth VII, 1 (43ᵃ) לפתן Mishnah (Talmud ed. לפתם), explained ib. 43ᵇ לפתא דדמי וכ׳ (read ם … or … ן), see גַּרְגְּלִידָא.
מַקָּבָן m. (denominative of מַקָּב) one whose head is mallet-shaped. Bekhoroth VII, 1, see מַקָּבָא.

מוּם m. (Biblical Hebrew; = מְאוּם; see מָה,
1) something, anything. Nedarim 66ᵇ, see יָפֶה.—Yerushalmi Kiddushin III, 64ᶜ bottom of page מהו ממזר מום זר what is mamzer (מַמְזֵר)? Something repulsive; Yevamot 76ᵇ ממזר כתיב מ׳ זר the Law says mamzer which means anything repulsive (male or female); Sifré Devarim 248 כל שהוא מומזר (correct accordingly) whatever is in any way repulsive.

—2) blemish. Bekhoroth V, 5, and from בעל מ׳ having a blemish (unfit for the altar, for priestly service &c.). Ib. VI, 9, and from הרי זה מ׳ this is a legal blemish; אינה מ׳ this is not &c.—Megillah 29ᵃ, see יָהִיר. Bava Metzia 59ᵇ מ׳ שבך וכ׳ do not reproach thy neighbor with a fault which is also thine own; and from—plural מוּמִין. Bekhoroth VI, 1 על אלו מ׳ וכ׳ these are the blemishes in consequence of which a first-born animal may be slaughtered (after the destruction of the Temple). Ib. 2 אין מ׳ בלבן a blemish in the white of the eye is no blemish in the sense of the law. Ib. VII, 1 מ׳ אלו … פוסלין וכ׳ the above named blemishes, whether permanent or transitory, make also human beings unfit (for priesthood &c.); and from—Denom. הוּמָם to become blemished, defective. Yerushalmi Shekalim IV, 48ᵇ שפודין תמימין והוּמְמוּ they had redeemed them when they were without blemish, and they became blemished. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 12, end; Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VI, 4 ולא הוממו וכ׳ and they have not become unfit for sacrifices on account of blemishes or old age &c., see זָהַם.—Yerushalmi Yoma II, 39ᵈ קטורת שכבת הוּמָמָה frankincense which was extinguished is unfit for the altar.

סְקִיפַס, שְׁקִי׳ m. (denominative of סְקִיף or שְׁקוֹף) one whose occiput has the shape of a lintel (having an angular projection). Bekhoroth VII, 1 (43ᵃ) (Mishnah and Arukh ש׳). Ib. 43ᵇ ס׳ מאחוריו וכ׳ s’ḳifas refers to the hinder part of the head, as people say ש̇ק̇יל פ̇יס̇א, a piece is taken off.

שָׁקַע (Biblical Hebrew)
1) to be depressed, sink, go down. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. III, 42ᶜ bottom of page אם היה חותמה שׁוֹקֵעַ if the seal on it was engraven, opposed בולט; Tosefta Pirkei Avot Zar. V (VI), 2; Bavli Pirkei Avot Zar. 43ᵇ. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 19 (reference. to לרוח היום, Breishit III, 8) לרוח ששׁוֹקַעַת עם היום by the (western) wind that goes down with the day. Ib. כל שהיום שוקע וכ׳ the more the day goes down, the cooler it grows. Yerushalmi Shabbat I, 3ᵈ top אחד צף ואחד שוקע וכ׳ one kind of poison floats, another settles &c. Mikvaot X, 1 צלוחית שפיה שוקע a bottle the mouth of which is turned down. Menachot 103ᵇ, see Hithpaël; and from

—2) to sink, let down. Bava Metzia V, 7 מששְׁקָעוֹ בכבשן after he let the lime stones down into the kiln (Yerushalmi ed. משיִשְׁקַע כבשנו, or משיְשַׁקֵּעַ) when he has filled his kiln). Yalkut Kohelet 966, see שָׁלָה; and e.—Part. pass. שָׁקוּעַ; f. שְׁקוּעָה &c. Bekhoroth 43ᵇ, see חָרַם. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 1522 והארץ ש׳ במים the earth was submerged in water. Sifra Thazr., Parah 5, Chaldaic XV (reference. to פחתת, Vayikra XIII, 55) שיהיו כל מראיה שְׁקוּעִין Rabad (ed. שׁוֹקְעִין) that all its colors appear lower (see שַׁקִּיעַ; compare עָמוֹק); Yalkut Vayikra 553 שׁוֹקְעִין; and e.—Bekhoroth VII, 1 ראשו ש׳, see שָׁקוּט.

Piël - שִׁיקֵּעַ to sink, let down. Sanhedrin VI, 4 מְשַׁקְּעִין את הקורה וכ׳ they insert the trunk (of the gallows) in the ground. Yerushalmi Shekalim V, end, 49ᵇ כמה ממון שִׁיקְּעוּ אבותי כאן how much money have my ancestors sunk here (in building that synagogue)!; כמה נפשות שיקעו וכ׳ how many souls did thy ancestors sink here! were there no people to study the Law (on whom that money might have been spent)?; Yerushalmi Peah VIII, end, 21ᵇ. Bava Metzia V, 7 Yerushalmi ed., see supra; and e.—Transferred toembody in a collection without regard to original wording, to edit, abridge. Yerushalmi Horayot III, 48ᶜ top; Yerushalmi Shabbat XVI, 15ᶜ הדא דאת אמר עד שלא ש׳ בו רבי רוב משניות אבל משש׳ וכ׳ what you say (that the study of the Mishnah collection is preferable) refers to the time before Rabbi had embodied and abridged most of the Mishnayoth in his edition, but since then, run at all times after the Talmud (where the discussions are quoted in their original form).—Part. pass. מְשׁוּקָּע; f. מְשׁוּקַּעַת; plural מְשׁוּקָּעִים, מְשׁוּקָּעִין; מְשׁוּקָּעוֹת. Kohelet Rabbah to I, 15 מקצתה מש׳ בארץ part of the boat rests on dry land. Yerushalmi Bava Metzia II, beginning 8ᵇ במש׳ בו when the objeot is found stuck in it, opposed בנתון בו when it is seen that it was put there. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 33 שהיתה התיבה מש׳ במים וכ׳ that the ark was eleven cubits in the water. Yerushalmi Yoma VII, beginning 44ᵃ זרעו של דוד מש׳ שם the seed of David is sunk there (in the family of the Resh Galutha). Yerushalmi Shabbat III, 6ᵃ top כסא שרגליו מש׳ בטיט a chair the feet of which stick in the mud. Yerushalmi Chagigah I, 76ᵈ top; Yerushalmi Peah II, 17ᵃ כמה … וכולהן מש׳ במשנה many Hălakhoth have been communicated to Moses from Sinai, and they all are embodied in the Mishnah; and e.

Hifil - הִשְׁקִיעַ to sink, let down. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 68 ה׳ הקב"ה גלגל וכ׳ the Lord caused the sun to set before its time. Ib. מה אתה בצאתך הִשְׁקַעְתִּי חמה וכ׳ as I caused the sun to set when thou didst go out &c. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 21; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Aḥăre, p. 176ᵃ לעולם יַשְׁקִיעַ וכ׳ (Arukh section (Parashah) see רתק: יְשַׁקֵּעַ or יִשְׁקַע) man should at all times sink himself into the study of the Mishnah, for when he knocks &c., see רָתַק. Kohelet Rabbah to I, 5 עד שלא ה׳ שמשו … הזריח וכ׳ before God made the sun of Moses to set, he made the sun of Joshua to rise, see שֶׁמֶשׁ. Ib. 4 היוצר הזה מַשְׁקִיעַ כבשונו מה שמשקיע וכ׳ the potter fills his oven; what he sinks into it first, is the last to come out; and from

Hithpaël - הִשְׁתַּקֵּע,

Nithpaël - נִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ
1) to be sunk, drowned; to be mixed up beyond recognition. Midrash Till. to Psalms XXII המִשְׁתַּקְּעִים שוקעים את שוקעיהן those that were to be drowned, drowned those that wanted to drown them. Ruth Rabbah to I, 17 נ׳ … בחליו was three days unconscious on his sick-bed, opposed נתישבה דעתו he came to. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 156 מִשְׁתַּקְּעִין בעונות וכ׳ are sunk in sins through the evil inclination. Ib.15 עד שנִשְׁתַּקְּעוּ תהומות until the depths were filled with water. Yerushalmi Shekalim VIII, beginning 51ᵃ והיו עולי רגלים משתקעין וכ׳ the pilgrims sank in blood up to their knees; Menachot 103ᵇ שוקעין; Tosefta Eduy. III, 2 מפקיעין בדם וכ׳ ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (read: מְשׁוּקָּעִין; Variant מְשַׁקְּעִין את ארכובותיהן). Arakhin 6ᵇ עד שלא נ׳ שם וכ׳ as long as the name of its owner (that donated it) is not merged (but is still traceable). Kiddushin 75ᵃ עד שיִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ שם ע"א ממנו until the name of idolatry has disappeared from him (until his idolatrous ancestry is no longer traceable). Yerushalmi Ketubot I, 25ᵈ top משפחה שנ׳ בה פסול וכ׳ if a genealogical blemish is mixed up in a family, you must investigate it back to four mothers; Yerushalmi Kiddushin IV, 65ᵈ bottom of page Ib. מה נאשה ונִשְׁתַּקְּעוּ בהן גדולי הדור what can we do (with these families), since prominent men of the generation are mixed up with them? Ib. חמשת … וכולם נשתקעו בכהונה וכ׳ Pashhur ben Imer had five thousand slaves, and they are all mixed up with high priestly families; Yerushalmi Yevamot VIII, 9ᵈ top; (Kiddushin 70ᵇ נטמעו). Midrash Tanḥuma Noah 5 the Lord supported Noah שלא יִשְׁתַּקֵּעַ במעשה דור המבול lest he sink down in (the mud of) the deeds of the generation of the flood; and from

—2) to settle permanently, be naturalized. Sifré Devarim 301 (reference. to Devarim XXVI, 5 ויגר) מלמד … להִשְׁתַּקֵּע אלא לגור שם this shows that he (Jacob) did not go down (to Egypt) to settle there as a citizen, but only to sojourn there.

—3) to be lost in forests, fields &c. Yerushalmi Berakhot II, end, 5ᵈ ובשעה שהוא משתקע וכ׳ but when one is lost, he may even trespass on a field of crocus; (Bava Kamma 81ᵃ תועה). Yerushalmi Berakhot l. common gender.; Yerushalmi Bava Batra V, 15ᵃ bottom of page וראו … משתקע ובא כנגדן they saw R. J. b. P. having lost his way and coming (through fields) towards them.

comments.en: These blemishes (i.e., those mentioned above as to animals), whether permanent or transitory, are disqualifying in a person (i.e., a priest serving in the Temple) (Bekh. 7:1). In addition to those, [there are certain defects that are only considered blemishes] in a person: One whose neck is short or narrow, those who have leaky [eyes], those who are bald, and those who have no teeth. Those who are hump-backed are fit [to serve], but they are [nonetheless treated as] disqualified because of their appearance. A eunuch by man and a eunuch by nature; one whose member is wounded, crushed, or severed; the shachniah; and the sagris [are all disqualified]. What is a shachniah? One whose eyebrows lie flat (i.e., thereby covering his eyes). A sagris? One who has one black eyebrow and one white. What is a sakei shemesh (Bekh. 7:3)? One who can see the room and the attic at the same time.
comments.he: מומין אלו בין קבועין ובין עוברין פסולין באדם יתר עליהן אדם צוארו שמוט ושקוע הזבלגנים והקרחנין ושאין להן שינים בעלי חטוטרות כשרים אבל פסולין מפני מראית העין סריס אדם וסריס חמה פצוע דכא וכרות שפכה השכניה והסגריס. איזה הוא שכניה שגביניו שוכבין. סגריס שגביניו אחד שחור ואחד לבן. איזהו הוא סכי שמש שרואה את החדר ואת העלייה כאחת. לראות אחד רואה שנים הא כיצד ראה את חברו והוא אומר לא רואה. חוטמו בלום וסולד ונוטף. אזניו רצומות ואזניו רצועות ועיניו טרוטות ועיניו מלודניות ועיניו גדולות או קטנות. גדולות כשל עגל קטנות כשל אווז ובעל בוהקית רוח קצרית באה עליו ובין הנפלים באה עליו נכפה אפילו לזמן מרובה.

sections.en: Concerning these blemishes which were taught with regard to an animal, whether they are permanent or transient, they also disqualify in the case of a person, i.e., they disqualify a priest from performing the Temple service. And in addition to those blemishes, there are other blemishes that apply only to a priest: One whose head is pointed, narrow above and wide below; and one whose head is turnip-like, wide above and narrow below; and one whose head is hammer-like, with his forehead protruding; and one whose head has an indentation; and one wherein the back of his head protrudes. And with regard to those with humped backs, Rabbi Yehuda deems them fit for service and the Rabbis deem them disqualified.
sections.he: מוּמִין אֵלּוּ, בֵּין קְבוּעִין בֵּין עוֹבְרִין, פּוֹסְלִין בָּאָדָם. יוֹתֵר עֲלֵיהֶן בָּאָדָם, הַכִּילוֹן, וְהַלַּפְתָּן, הַמַּקָּבָן, וְשֶׁרֹאשׁוֹ שָׁקוּעַ, וּשְׁקִיפָס. וּבַעֲלֵי הַחֲטוֹטֶרֶת, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַכְשִׁיר, וַחֲכָמִים פּוֹסְלִין:

en: גְּבִין II m. h. (see גַּב) eye-brow. Niddah 23ᵇ הגבין Arukh (ed. הגבן correct accordingly). Bekhoroth VII, 2 (43ᵇ) אין לו גבינין … אלא ג׳ אחד וכ׳ if one has no eye-brows or only one eye-brow,—this is the gibben of the Bible (Vayikra XXI, 20); explained Ib. ib. זהו מדרש או גבן this is what is deducted by interpretation from ô gibben (ib.).—plural גְּבִינִים, גְּבִינִין. Niddah l. common gender.; Yerushalmi ib. III, 50ᶜ bottom of page—Bekhoroth l. common gender., see supra. Ib. (explain. גִּבֵּן, Vayikra l. common gender.) שגְּבִינָיו שוכבין (not שגבינין) whose eye-brows are lying (overshadowing the eyes).

גִּבֵּן m. (Biblical Hebrew, denominative of גַּב) hump-backed, or one having defective eye-brows. Bekhoroth VII, 2 R. Ḥanina … says, the gibben of the Bible (Vayikra XXI, 20) is מי שיש לו שני גבים וכ׳, see גַּב h.; oth. opinion, see section (Parashah) see גְּבִין. [Targ. Yerushalmi II extremely tall, see גְּבִיחַ.]

גַּב m. (Biblical Hebrew; גבב) convex, arched, whence
1) the exterior or upper part of a thing, a) body, especially back (of an animal’s body, usually אָחוֹר). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 8, beginning he split the double-faced body (see פרצוף) ועשאו גַּבַּיִים ג׳ לכאן וכ׳ and gave it two backs, one back on this side &c.—גַּב יָד, גַּב רֶגֶל a swelling on the hand, on the foot. Pirkei Avot Zar. 28ᵃ; Shabbat 109ᵃ.—b) eye-brow (Biblical Hebrew), the elevation around genitals &c. Niddah 52ᵇ א׳ בגַבָּהּ one hair on the lower surrounding of her genitals, opposed בכריסה, see כֶּרֶס; Bava Batra 56ᵇ; Sanhedrin 30ᵇ; Bava Kamma 70ᵇ, [Rashi: on her finger joints].—c) (also גַּבָּה) גַּבַּת הַזָּקֵן, plural גַּבּוֹת, chin. Niddah 23ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. III, 50ᶜ bottom of page גומות הזקן (dimples).—*d) a low fence. Tosefta Bava Metzia XI, 22 (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) גַּג).—Dual גַּבַּיִים, גַּבַּיִין. Kelim XXV, 5 outsides of vessels (usually אֲחוֹרַיִים). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 8, see supra.—plural גַּבִּים, גַּבִּין, גַּבּוֹת. Bekhoroth VII, 2 שני ג׳ וכ׳ double back and double spine (explain. גִּבֵּן, Vayikra XXI, 20); Niddah 24ᵃ sq.; Chullin 60ᵇ.—Niddah 23ᵇ ג׳ הזקן, see supra.—עַל גַּב, עַל גַּבֵּי (abbr. ע"ג) on, upon, by the side of (compare עַל in Biblical Hebrew). Chullin 3ᵃ, and from עומד על גַּבָּיו standing by him, superintending. Niddah 66ᵃ על גב הנהר by the river-side; Makhshirin I, 4 (see גֵּיף). Sukkah IV, 4 על גב איצטבא (Talmud ed. 42ᵇ גבי), see אִיסְטְבָא.—Transferred on the basis, on the principle. אף על גב, see אַף I.—Yerushalmi Chagigah II, 78ᵇ bottom of page חולין שנעשו על גב הקדש (usually על טהרת הקדש) layman’s food prepared on the principles of sacred food (as though it were sacred food). Beitzah II, 3 (17ᵇ); Tosefta ib. II, 7 מטבילין מגב לגב you may (on a Holy Day) immerse vessels for the purpose of changing their use (literally: from principle to principle, from one על גב to another); explained ibid. רצה לעשות גיתו ע"ג בדו ובדו ע"ג עיסתו הרי זה וכ׳ if one desires to work his wine press on the basis of his olive press, i.e. with vessels originally immersed for the use of the olive press, or his olive press on the basis of his dough, i.e. with vessels originally immersed to be used for kneading, he may immerse his vessels on the same day; Beitzah 19ᵃ ע"ג בדו ובדו ע"ג גיתו עושה … Manuscript Munich and Arukh (ed. incorr. כדו) if one wishes to change &c., he might have done so (even without another immersion and, therefore, may re-immerse his vessels on the Holy Day because he does not thereby create a new status).—Cmp. אַגַּב.—Tosefta Shabbat XII (XIII), 1; Yerushalmi ib. XIII, 14ᵃ top ע"ג הגס וכ׳ around, or adding to the border of a web &c.; Bavli ib. 105ᵃ על הגס. Horayot III, 3 אין על גַּבָּיו אלא וכ׳ none over him save the Lord his God.—בְּגַב in the back, behind. Yerushalmi Ketubot XII, 35ᵇ top דברים בגב (Bavli ib. 111ᵃ בגו) there is something behind, i.e. there is a reason for it.—Cmp. כַּף.

קֵרֵחַ m. (Biblical Hebrew; see next word) bald, bald head. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 65, see קִיוֵּוץ. Bekhoroth VII, 2 הק׳ פסול a bald-headed person is unfit for priestly functions; איזה ק׳ כל וכ׳ bald-headed (in a legal sense) is he who has not a line of hair from ear to ear. Ib. 58ᵃ הק׳ הזה that bald head (R. Akiba). Bava Kamma 60ᵇ נמצא ק׳ מכאן וק׳ מכאן finally he is bald from here and bald from there (has neither white nor black hair); and from—Gittin VIII, 9, and e. גט ק׳ a letter of divorce that lacks signatures on each of its folds (see קָשַׁר).—plural קֵרְחִים, קֵרְחִין. Yerushalmi Yoma II, end, 40ᵃ הכהנים לרבות הק׳ ‘the priests’ (Vayikra I, 5), this includes the bald heads (as fit for that function); Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., Parah 4, Chaldaic VI קַרְחָנִים; Bekhoroth 43ᵇ קרְחָנִין.—Fem. קֵרַחַת. Bava Batra 132ᵃ ק׳ מכאן ומכאן she is bald on both sides, i.e. has forfeited both claims on her husband’s estate.

שִׁדְרָה, שִׁי׳ f. (see שְׁדַר II) [twisted cord,]
1) spinal column. Chullin III, 2 נשברה הש׳ ולא וכ׳ if the spinal column is broken, but its cord is not severed. Ib. 1. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 28, beginning, and e. לוז של ש׳, see לוּז II. Shabbat 147ᵇ חומרי ש׳ Rashi (ed. שדרא) the knots of the spine(vertebræ). Oholot I, 8, see חוּלְיָא I; and from—Bava Kamma 16ᵃ שִׁדְרוֹ של אדם a man’s spine. Berakhot 55ᵃ; Shabbat 81ᵃ שדרו של דג the back-bone of a fish.—plural שִׁדְרָאוֹת. Niddah 24ᵃ; Bekhoroth VII, 2; Chullin 60ᵇ, see גַּב.

—2) stem, rib of a plant. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 30 הש׳ של לולב דומה לש׳ וכ׳ the rib of the palm-branch resembles the spinal column of man. ‘'Uktzin I, 2 הש׳ של שבולת the stem of an ear (of wheat). Chullin 119ᵇ בש׳ it refers to the stem of an ear of wheat, see שֹׁומֵר; and from—V. שִׁזְרָה.

שָׁכַב (Biblical Hebrew) to incline; to lie down, lie, sleep. Bekhoroth VII, 2, and e. גביניו שׁוֹכְבִין, see גְּבִין II. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 96 (reference. to Breishit XLVII, 28 sq.) אתה שׁוֹכֵב ואין אתה מת thou shalt lie (in the grave) but not be dead (forever). Berakhot I, 3 (reference. to Devarim VI, 9) בשעה … שׁוֹכְבִים וכ׳ (you must read the Sh’mʿa) at the time of the day when people lie down, and when people get up. Ib. 62ᵇ על כל משכב שְׁכַב וכ׳ lie on any couch, only not on the bare ground; and see from—Part. pass. שָׁכוּב. Mekhilta Beshalach, Vayassʿa, section (Parashah) 3 תפלתם … שהיו שְׁכוּבִים בעפר the prayer of our fathers who were asleep in the ground; Yalkut Shemot 260 שוכבין.

Hifil - הִשְׁכִּיב
1) to cause to lie down. Berakhot 60ᵇ (in a night prayer) שתַּשְׁכִּיבֵנִי לשלום וכ׳ that thou make me to lie down for peace and to rise for peace &c. Berakhot 4ᵇ הַשְׁכִּיבֵנוּ (cause us to lie down,) hashkibenu, a section of the evening prayers, inserted between G’ullah and T’fillah (see גְּאוּלָּה). Ib. 9ᵇ; and from

—2) to let lie with, to allow sodomy. Keritot 3ᵃ (reference. to Vayikra XVIII, 22) קרי ביה לא תַשְׁכִּיב read it as lo thashkib, do not allow &c.; Sanhedrin 54ᵇ לא תַשְׁכֵּב (or תִשָּׁכֵב Nifal); and e.

Nifal - נִשְׁכַּב to be lain with, especially to be the subject of sodomy. Ib. אזהרה לנִשְׁכָּב מנין whence do we derive the warning (אַזְהָרָה) for the person that allows sodomy? Ib. [read:] לר׳ ישמעאל אזהרה לנ׳ לבהמה וכ׳ (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 200, and Yalkut Vayikra 599) according to R. Yishmael’s interpretation, whence do we derive the warning for the person that is made the subject of coupling with a beast? Ib. לא תִשָּׁכֵב, see supra; and from

comments.en: 12) (Vayikra 21:20) ("Or one who is gibein or dak or tevalul in his eye; or one who is garav or yalefeth or meroach ashech.") "gibein": one who has two eyebrows (that are fused). Whence do I derive from inclusion one who has no eyebrows or only one? From "or gibein." R. Dossa says ("Gibein refers to) one whose brows droop (over his eyes.) R. Chanina b. Antignos Says ("Gibein refers to) one who has two backs and two spines. "dak": This is cataract. Whence do I derive for inclusion chilazon, nachash, and einav? From "or dak."
comments.he: [יב] "גבן" – שיש לו גבינים הרבה. אין לו גבינים או אין לו אלא גבן אחד, זה גבן האמור בתורה. ר' דוסא אומר, מי שגביניו שוכבים. ר' חנינא בן אנטיגנוס אומר, כל שיש לו שתי גבים ושתי שדראות. "דק" – זה הדוק. חלזון נחש, עינב מנין? תלמוד לומר "או דק".

comments.en: These blemishes (i.e., those mentioned above as to animals), whether permanent or transitory, are disqualifying in a person (i.e., a priest serving in the Temple) (Bekh. 7:1). In addition to those, [there are certain defects that are only considered blemishes] in a person: One whose neck is short or narrow, those who have leaky [eyes], those who are bald, and those who have no teeth. Those who are hump-backed are fit [to serve], but they are [nonetheless treated as] disqualified because of their appearance. A eunuch by man and a eunuch by nature; one whose member is wounded, crushed, or severed; the shachniah; and the sagris [are all disqualified]. What is a shachniah? One whose eyebrows lie flat (i.e., thereby covering his eyes). A sagris? One who has one black eyebrow and one white. What is a sakei shemesh (Bekh. 7:3)? One who can see the room and the attic at the same time.
comments.he: מומין אלו בין קבועין ובין עוברין פסולין באדם יתר עליהן אדם צוארו שמוט ושקוע הזבלגנים והקרחנין ושאין להן שינים בעלי חטוטרות כשרים אבל פסולין מפני מראית העין סריס אדם וסריס חמה פצוע דכא וכרות שפכה השכניה והסגריס. איזה הוא שכניה שגביניו שוכבין. סגריס שגביניו אחד שחור ואחד לבן. איזהו הוא סכי שמש שרואה את החדר ואת העלייה כאחת. לראות אחד רואה שנים הא כיצד ראה את חברו והוא אומר לא רואה. חוטמו בלום וסולד ונוטף. אזניו רצומות ואזניו רצועות ועיניו טרוטות ועיניו מלודניות ועיניו גדולות או קטנות. גדולות כשל עגל קטנות כשל אווז ובעל בוהקית רוח קצרית באה עליו ובין הנפלים באה עליו נכפה אפילו לזמן מרובה.

comments.en: or who is a hunchback, or a dwarf, or who has a growth in his eye, or who has a boil-scar, or scurvy, or crushed testes.
comments.he: אֽוֹ־גִבֵּ֣ן אוֹ־דַ֔ק א֖וֹ תְּבַלֻּ֣ל בְּעֵינ֑וֹ א֤וֹ גָרָב֙ א֣וֹ יַלֶּ֔פֶת א֖וֹ מְר֥וֹחַ אָֽשֶׁךְ׃

sections.en: The kere’aḥ is disqualified from performing the Temple service. What is a kere’aḥ? It is anyone who does not have a row of hair encircling his head from ear to ear. If he has a row of hair from ear to ear, that person is fit for service. If a priest has no eyebrows, or if he has only one eyebrow, that is the gibben that is stated in the Torah in the list of blemished priests (see Leviticus 21:20). Rabbi Dosa says: A gibben is one whose eyebrows are so long that they lie flat and cover his eyes. Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says: A gibben is one who has two backs and two spines.
sections.he: הַקֵּרֵחַ, פָּסוּל. אֵיזֶהוּ קֵרֵחַ, כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שִׁטָּה שֶׁל שֵׂעָר מַקֶּפֶת מֵאֹזֶן לְאֹזֶן. וְאִם יֵשׁ לוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה כָּשֵׁר. אֵין לוֹ גְבִּינִים, אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא גְבִין אֶחָד, הוּא גִבֵּן הָאָמוּר בַּתּוֹרָה. רַבִּי דוֹסָא אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁגְּבִּינָיו שׁוֹכְבִין. רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי גַבִּים וּשְׁתֵּי שִׁדְרָאוֹת:

en: זַגְדּוּם, זַגְדָּן, (זוּגְדֵּס) m. (contr. of זוּג and גד from גדד, compare גדודא juvenis cælebs, Payne Smith, Thesaurus Syriacus 652) unmatched; especially one with an unequal pair of eyes or eye-brows. Bekhoroth VII, 3 זוגדס Mishnah (see infra; Talmud ed. 43ᵇ זגדן). Ib. 44ᵃ זגדום אחד שחור וכ׳ Z. is one who has one black and one white eye-brow; כל זוגא … ז׳ קרי ליה any unequal pair is called Z. Ib. זַגְדָּיָיא מחוי וכ׳ (Chaldaic form of our word); Tosefta ib. V, 2, sq. סגריס (read: סַגְדּוּם Safel of גדד). Sifra Emor Chaldaic II, Parah 3 זגדיס (read … ם). [Ar. זגדוס, influenced by the etymol.: זוג, and דּוּס = δίς.]

חָרַם (Biblical Hebrew) [to perforate, break through (compare Arab. ḫaram, and חֲרָךְ I),]
1) to make a net. Menachot 37ᵃ top ר׳ יוסי החוֹרֵם R. J. the net-maker (or fisher); [Rashi, reading החָרוּם, (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l., note 100), see infra].

—2) to perforate. Part. pass. חָרוּם (Biblical Hebrew חָרֻם) one whose nose is so flattened as to show its holes, flat-nosed. Bekhoroth VII, 3 איזהו ח׳ הכוחל וכ׳ a ḥarum is he who can paint both of his eyes with one movement. Ib. 43ᵇ ח׳ שחוטמו שקוע ḥ. is one whose nose is sunk.

—3) to cut off, to set outside (compare Arab. ḥaram), see infra, and חֵרֶם.—[
4) to burn, compare חָרַךְ, חָרֵב; see חוּרְמַן.]

Hifil - הֶחֱרִים (denominative of חֵרֶם) [to set outside, apart,]
1) to dedicate for priestly or sacred use (Vayikra XXVII, 28, sq.); to renounce private use. Arakhin VIII, 4 מַחֲרִים אדם וכ׳ a man may renounce a portion of his sheep &c.; ואם ה׳ את כולם אינן מוּחֲרָמִין but if he renounces all of them, they are not dedicated (his vow is invalid). Ib. מה אם לגבוה להַחֲרִים וכ׳ since man is not permitted to renounce all his property even for a sacred purpose &c. Ib. 7 מח׳ אדם את קדשיו וכ׳ one may declare ḥerem one’s own designated offerings (in which case he has to pay their value to the priest or the sanctuary); and see from—Part. pass. מוּחֳרָם, plural מוּחֳרָמִין, מוּחֳרָמִים. Ib. 4, sq., see supra; and from

—2) to excommunicate, to pronounce the higher ban (which includes the withdrawal of protection of property). Moʿed Katan 16ᵃ מנדין … ומַחֲרִימִין וכ׳ the smaller ban is pronounced (over one disregarding a legal summons) at once …, the great ban after sixty days.

מַרְאִית f. (רָאָה), מ׳ (ה)עין, appearance, sight, semblance. Bekhoroth VII, 3 מפני מ׳ הע׳ because he is repulsive to look at. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 26; Midrash Till. to Psalms VII אינו מוליך … מפני מ׳ הע׳ he does not take his children with him, because he is afraid of the evil eye.—Esp. מפני מ׳ (ה)ע׳ in order to avoid the semblance of wrong-doing, for appearance sake. Beitzah 9ᵃ, and from כל מקום שאסרו חכמים מפני מ׳ הע׳ אפי׳ וכ׳ wherever the scholars have forbidden a thing for appearance sake, it is forbidden even in strictest privacy, compare חֶדֶר; Yerushalmi Eruvin VIII, end, 25ᵇ. Yerushalmi Moʿed Katan I, 80ᵇ. ולית לרבנן מפני מ׳ ע׳ do the Rabbis not care for appearance?; and from

סָכֵי m. (preceding) סְכֵי שמש looking to the sun, euphem. for squinting, cross-eyed. Tosefta Bekhoroth V, 3, explained שרואה את החדר וכ׳ who takes in the room and the ceiling in one glance; Bekhoroth VII, 3, changed by R. Jose. ib. 44ᵃ: סני שמש one who hates the sun, blinkard

עַיִן f. (Biblical Hebrew; עוּן)
1) eye, sight, look. Kiddushin 24ᵃ בשן וע׳, see יָצָא. Ib. 24ᵇ הכהו על עֵינוֹ וכ׳ if the master struck him on his eye and made it blind. Bava Kamma 83ᵇ (reference. to Shemot XXI, 24) אימא ע׳ ממש may not the text mean that he who injures a person’s eye must really suffer the same injury? Shabbat 108ᵇ bottom of page יד לע׳ וכ׳ an unwashed hand (in the morning) touching the eye deserves to be cut off. Taanit 8ᵇ סמוי מן הע׳, see סָמָא. Ib. דבר שאין הע׳ שולטת בו something which the eye cannot look at (being stored away), see infra; and see from—[Yerushalmi Nedarim IX, end, 41ᶜ עשה לה ע׳ של זהב, a corrupt dittography of עשה לה שן של זהב.]—ע׳ טובה (also יפה) a benevolent eye, good will, liberality, opposed ע׳ רעה or עֵין הרע (abbr. עה"ר), also ע׳ צרה ill-will, selfishness, envy. Pirkei Avot II, 9. Shabbat 74ᵃ משום ע׳ יפה וכ׳ he intended to show his good will. Tosefta Hallah I, 7 שעינו יפה בעיסתו he is liberal with his dough (is glad to give the priest’s portion), opposed עינו צרה. Esther Rabbah to I, 4 היתה עינו צרה בממונו he was jealous of his wealth (unwilling to leave it to his heirs to be enjoyed by them). Pirkei Avot V, 13 עינו רצה בשל אחרים he is illiberal with regard to other people’s money (begrudges them the privilege of giving charity), ע׳ רעה בשלו he is illiberal with his own money (is too greedy to afford himself the pleasure of giving charity). Ib. II, 11, see יֵצֶר; and from—צַר ע׳ (= רַע ע׳) selfish, opposed טוב ע׳ liberal, selfless. Shabbat 108ᵇ שדורי … צר ע׳ אנא I send you (the salve), lest you say that I am selfish. Sotah 38ᵇ אפי׳ העופות מכירין בצָרֵי ע׳ even birds recognize selfish men. Ib. כל הנהנה מצרי ע׳ וכ׳ he who accepts benefits from self-seeking men, transgresses a law (reference. to Mishlei XXIII, 6). Ib. אין … לטוב ע׳ the cup of benediction must be handed to none but an unselfish person (with reference. to Mishlei XXII, 9); and e.—Esp. ע׳ רעה, עֵין הרע (abbrev. עה"ר), or only עַיִן, the evil eye, an envious glance that brings harm to the person looked at, bewitchment. Bava Metzia 107ᵇ (reference. to Devarim VII, 15) זו ע׳ that means the effect of an evil eye. Ib. תשעים … בע׳ רעה וכ׳ ninety-nine persons die of an evil eye against one in the natural course. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 91 שלא תשלוט בכם עה"ר that the evil eye may have no power over you. Ib. לא הייתם … מפני הע׳ were you not afraid of the evil eye? Berakhot 20a ע׳ שלא … אין עה"ר שולטת בי no evil eye can affect him whose eye refused to feed on what was not his (to look at the charms of a married woman); and from—שקל ע׳ בע׳ to balance the scales exactly, to allow no overweight (see עוּן, and כָּרַע). Bava Batra V, 11; and from—בע׳ visible to the eye, discernible; in natural form. Yerushalmi Berakhot VI, 10ᵃ אע"פ ששחוקין בעֵינָן הן although they are ground, they are still discernible. Ib. אם בעַיְינָן הן if they are in their natural form (not mashed); and from—כְּעֵין like the appearance of, similar to, a sort of (compare גַּוָּון). Ib.ᵇ כל שהוא כע׳ סולת וכ׳ whatever resembles a pudding or dumpling. Berakhot 58ᵃ (in Chald. dict.) מלכותא דארעא כע׳ וכ׳ the government on earth is like the government in heaven (inspires reverence); and from—מֵעֵין a reflection of, of the nature of; an abstract of. Sanhedrin 105ᵇ (reference. to the preposition מ in I Kings I, 47) מע׳ קאמר ליה he means, ‘as a reflection’ (of thy name, thy throne). Ib. (reference. to Judges V, 24) מע׳ קאמר it means ‘similar to’ (the blessings of Sarah &c.). Berakhot IV, 3 מע׳ י"ח an abstract of the eighteen benedictions. Yerushalmi ib. 8ᵃ bottom of page שבע מע׳ י"ח seven benedictions embodying the eighteen. Ib. VI, 10ᵇ ברכה אחת מע׳ שלש one benediction embodying the three. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 11, and e., see דּוּגְמַטְרִין.—Dual עֵינַיִים, עֵינַיִם. Bekhoroth VII, 4 עֵינָיו גדולות וכ׳ if his (the priest’s) eyes are as large as those of a calf. Ib. 3. Berakhot 58ᵃ, and e. נתן עיניו בו וכ׳ he put his eyes on him, and he was turned into a heap of bones. Yerushalmi Horayot III, end, 48ᶜ נתנו עֵינֵיהֶן בשמואל וכ׳ they directed their attention to Samuel &c.; and from—אחז את הע׳, see אָחַז.

—2) anything resembling the eye, hole, ring &c. Kelim VIII, 7 ע׳ של תנור the ‘eye’ of an oven (the fire-place under the oven, Maimonides; the opening for the escape of the smoke, which may be closed to retain the heat, Rabbenu Shimshon). Ib. IX, 8 תנור שניקב מעינו an oven in the eye of which is a defect. Ib. XXI, 2 ע׳ the ring-shaped pad around an animal’s neck (a halter of soft material). Ib. ע׳ של מתכת a metal hame (compare עוֹנָתָא). Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 7 העיין שבמצעד the ring attached to an adze; and from

—3) spring, well. Ketubot I, 10; and from—[Frequ. עֵין in proper noun of a place, as ע׳ סוכר, ע׳ טב; see respective determinants].

צִירָן m. (denominative of צִיר I) one whose eyes discharge a briny liquid, blear-eyed; [Rashi: one whose eyes have a cylindrical shape like a pivot, from צִיר II]. Bekhoroth VII, 3, explained ib. 44ᵃ עיניו תרוטות וצִירָנִיּוֹת whose eyes are bleared and granulated; [Rashi: round or pivot-shaped]; Tosefta ib. V, 3 עיניו מצודניות ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (correct accordingly, or read with oth. ed. מְרוֹדָנִיּוֹת).

comments.en: 14) "in his eye": Any defect of the eye is implied. From here it is derived that if both his eyes were oriented upwards or downwards, if one eye were oriented upwards and the other downwards, if he saw the room or the attic as one, if he "hated the sun," if his eyes were unmatched, if he spoke with one person and gave the impression that he was looking at him [— all of these are considered blemishes).
comments.he: [יד] "בעינו" – להביא את שבעיניו: שתי עיניו למעלה, ושתי עיניו למטה, עינו אחת למעלה ועינו אחת למטה, ורואה את החדר ואת העליה כאחת, סני שמש, והזוגדן, והמדבר עם חבירו ואחר אומר "לי הוא רואה".

en: The mishna teaches that if both of one’s eyes are above or both of his eyes are below, he is disqualified from performing the Temple service. The Gemara asks: What does the mishna mean when it mentions a priest wherein both of his eyes are above or both of his eyes are below? If we say that the phrase: Both of his eyes are above, means that he constantly gazes upward, and the phrase: Both of his eyes are below, means that he constantly gazes downward, then the case where one of his eyes is above and one of his eyes is below must similarly mean that he gazes with one of his eyes downward and one of his eyes upward. But if so, this is identical to the next case in the mishna, that one sees both the room on the ground floor and the upper story as one.

Rather, the phrase: Both of his eyes are above, is referring to a case where his eyes are situated above their normal place, and the phrase: Both of his eyes are below, is referring to a case where his eyes are situated below their normal place. Similarly, the case where one of his eyes is above and one of his eyes is below is where one of his eyes is situated above and one of his eyes is situated below. And the mishna adds that in a case where his eyes are situated in their proper arrangement as well, but he sees the room on the ground floor and the upper story as one, he too is considered blemished.

The Gemara asks: From where are these matters derived? As the Sages taught in a baraita: The verse states with regard to blemishes that disqualify priests: “Or a cataract or a tevallul in his eye” (Leviticus 21:20). Since it is obvious that a cataract or a tevallul can occur only in one’s eyes, why does the verse state: In his eye? The term “in his eye” indicates that any blemish that is in his eye disqualifies him from performing the Temple service. From here the Sages stated: If both of his eyes are below or both of his eyes are above, or if one of his eyes is above and one of his eyes is below, or if he sees the room and the upper story as one, or if when he speaks with his friend another person says: He is looking at me, he is blemished and is disqualified from performing the Temple service.
he: שתי עיניו למטה: מה שתי עיניו למעלה שתי עיניו למטה אילימא שתי עיניו למעלה דחזי למעלה שתי עיניו למטה דחזי למטה עינו אחת למעלה ועינו אחת למטה דחזאי עינו אחת למטה ועינו אחת למעלה היינו רואה את החדר ואת העלייה כאחת
אלא שתי עיניו למעלה דקיימן למעלה שתי עיניו למטה דקיימן למטה עינו אחת למעלה ועינו אחת למטה דקיימי עינו אחת למעלה ועינו אחת למטה וקיימי כסדרן נמי ורואה את החדר ואת העלייה כאחת
מנא הני מילי דת"ר (ויקרא כא, כ) בעינו כל מה שבעינו מכאן אמרו שתי עיניו למטה שתי עיניו למעלה עינו אחת למעלה ועינו אחת למטה ורואה את החדר ואת העלייה כאחת או שמדבר עם חבירו ואחר אומר לי רואה

comments.en: These blemishes (i.e., those mentioned above as to animals), whether permanent or transitory, are disqualifying in a person (i.e., a priest serving in the Temple) (Bekh. 7:1). In addition to those, [there are certain defects that are only considered blemishes] in a person: One whose neck is short or narrow, those who have leaky [eyes], those who are bald, and those who have no teeth. Those who are hump-backed are fit [to serve], but they are [nonetheless treated as] disqualified because of their appearance. A eunuch by man and a eunuch by nature; one whose member is wounded, crushed, or severed; the shachniah; and the sagris [are all disqualified]. What is a shachniah? One whose eyebrows lie flat (i.e., thereby covering his eyes). A sagris? One who has one black eyebrow and one white. What is a sakei shemesh (Bekh. 7:3)? One who can see the room and the attic at the same time.
comments.he: מומין אלו בין קבועין ובין עוברין פסולין באדם יתר עליהן אדם צוארו שמוט ושקוע הזבלגנים והקרחנין ושאין להן שינים בעלי חטוטרות כשרים אבל פסולין מפני מראית העין סריס אדם וסריס חמה פצוע דכא וכרות שפכה השכניה והסגריס. איזה הוא שכניה שגביניו שוכבין. סגריס שגביניו אחד שחור ואחד לבן. איזהו הוא סכי שמש שרואה את החדר ואת העלייה כאחת. לראות אחד רואה שנים הא כיצד ראה את חברו והוא אומר לא רואה. חוטמו בלום וסולד ונוטף. אזניו רצומות ואזניו רצועות ועיניו טרוטות ועיניו מלודניות ועיניו גדולות או קטנות. גדולות כשל עגל קטנות כשל אווז ובעל בוהקית רוח קצרית באה עליו ובין הנפלים באה עליו נכפה אפילו לזמן מרובה.

sections.en: The ḥarum is disqualified from performing the Temple service. What is a ḥarum? It is one who can paint both of his eyes as one, with one brushstroke, because he has a sunken nose. If both of one’s eyes are above or both of his eyes are below; or if one of his eyes is above and one of his eyes is below; or if both eyes are in the proper place but he sees both the room on the ground floor and the upper story as one, at the same time; and likewise those unable to look at the sun; and one whose eyes are different; and one whose eyes tear constantly, these are disqualified from performing the Temple service. And one whose eyelashes have fallen out is disqualified from performing the Temple service due to the appearance of a blemish. Unlike the others listed in this mishna, who are disqualified by Torah law, one with this condition is not disqualified by Torah law. Rather, the Sages issued a decree prohibiting a priest with such a condition to perform the Temple service.
sections.he: הֶחָרוּם, פָּסוּל. אֵיזֶהוּ חָרוּם, הַכּוֹחֵל שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו כְּאֶחָת. שְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַעְלָה, וּשְׁתֵּי עֵינָיו לְמַטָּה, עֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַעְלָה, וְעֵינוֹ אַחַת לְמַטָּה, רוֹאֶה אֶת הַחֶדֶר וְאֶת הָעֲלִיָּה כְּאֶחָת, סָכֵי שֶׁמֶשׁ, זוּגְדוֹס, וְהַצִּירָן. וְשֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ רִיסֵי עֵינָיו, פָּסוּל, מִפְּנֵי מַרְאִית הָעָיִן:

en:
עַיִן f. (Biblical Hebrew; עוּן)
1) eye, sight, look. Kiddushin 24ᵃ בשן וע׳, see יָצָא. Ib. 24ᵇ הכהו על עֵינוֹ וכ׳ if the master struck him on his eye and made it blind. Bava Kamma 83ᵇ (reference. to Shemot XXI, 24) אימא ע׳ ממש may not the text mean that he who injures a person’s eye must really suffer the same injury? Shabbat 108ᵇ bottom of page יד לע׳ וכ׳ an unwashed hand (in the morning) touching the eye deserves to be cut off. Taanit 8ᵇ סמוי מן הע׳, see סָמָא. Ib. דבר שאין הע׳ שולטת בו something which the eye cannot look at (being stored away), see infra; and see from—[Yerushalmi Nedarim IX, end, 41ᶜ עשה לה ע׳ של זהב, a corrupt dittography of עשה לה שן של זהב.]—ע׳ טובה (also יפה) a benevolent eye, good will, liberality, opposed ע׳ רעה or עֵין הרע (abbr. עה"ר), also ע׳ צרה ill-will, selfishness, envy. Pirkei Avot II, 9. Shabbat 74ᵃ משום ע׳ יפה וכ׳ he intended to show his good will. Tosefta Hallah I, 7 שעינו יפה בעיסתו he is liberal with his dough (is glad to give the priest’s portion), opposed עינו צרה. Esther Rabbah to I, 4 היתה עינו צרה בממונו he was jealous of his wealth (unwilling to leave it to his heirs to be enjoyed by them). Pirkei Avot V, 13 עינו רצה בשל אחרים he is illiberal with regard to other people’s money (begrudges them the privilege of giving charity), ע׳ רעה בשלו he is illiberal with his own money (is too greedy to afford himself the pleasure of giving charity). Ib. II, 11, see יֵצֶר; and from—צַר ע׳ (= רַע ע׳) selfish, opposed טוב ע׳ liberal, selfless. Shabbat 108ᵇ שדורי … צר ע׳ אנא I send you (the salve), lest you say that I am selfish. Sotah 38ᵇ אפי׳ העופות מכירין בצָרֵי ע׳ even birds recognize selfish men. Ib. כל הנהנה מצרי ע׳ וכ׳ he who accepts benefits from self-seeking men, transgresses a law (reference. to Mishlei XXIII, 6). Ib. אין … לטוב ע׳ the cup of benediction must be handed to none but an unselfish person (with reference. to Mishlei XXII, 9); and e.—Esp. ע׳ רעה, עֵין הרע (abbrev. עה"ר), or only עַיִן, the evil eye, an envious glance that brings harm to the person looked at, bewitchment. Bava Metzia 107ᵇ (reference. to Devarim VII, 15) זו ע׳ that means the effect of an evil eye. Ib. תשעים … בע׳ רעה וכ׳ ninety-nine persons die of an evil eye against one in the natural course. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 91 שלא תשלוט בכם עה"ר that the evil eye may have no power over you. Ib. לא הייתם … מפני הע׳ were you not afraid of the evil eye? Berakhot 20a ע׳ שלא … אין עה"ר שולטת בי no evil eye can affect him whose eye refused to feed on what was not his (to look at the charms of a married woman); and from—שקל ע׳ בע׳ to balance the scales exactly, to allow no overweight (see עוּן, and כָּרַע). Bava Batra V, 11; and from—בע׳ visible to the eye, discernible; in natural form. Yerushalmi Berakhot VI, 10ᵃ אע"פ ששחוקין בעֵינָן הן although they are ground, they are still discernible. Ib. אם בעַיְינָן הן if they are in their natural form (not mashed); and from—כְּעֵין like the appearance of, similar to, a sort of (compare גַּוָּון). Ib.ᵇ כל שהוא כע׳ סולת וכ׳ whatever resembles a pudding or dumpling. Berakhot 58ᵃ (in Chald. dict.) מלכותא דארעא כע׳ וכ׳ the government on earth is like the government in heaven (inspires reverence); and from—מֵעֵין a reflection of, of the nature of; an abstract of. Sanhedrin 105ᵇ (reference. to the preposition מ in I Kings I, 47) מע׳ קאמר ליה he means, ‘as a reflection’ (of thy name, thy throne). Ib. (reference. to Judges V, 24) מע׳ קאמר it means ‘similar to’ (the blessings of Sarah &c.). Berakhot IV, 3 מע׳ י"ח an abstract of the eighteen benedictions. Yerushalmi ib. 8ᵃ bottom of page שבע מע׳ י"ח seven benedictions embodying the eighteen. Ib. VI, 10ᵇ ברכה אחת מע׳ שלש one benediction embodying the three. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 11, and e., see דּוּגְמַטְרִין.—Dual עֵינַיִים, עֵינַיִם. Bekhoroth VII, 4 עֵינָיו גדולות וכ׳ if his (the priest’s) eyes are as large as those of a calf. Ib. 3. Berakhot 58ᵃ, and e. נתן עיניו בו וכ׳ he put his eyes on him, and he was turned into a heap of bones. Yerushalmi Horayot III, end, 48ᶜ נתנו עֵינֵיהֶן בשמואל וכ׳ they directed their attention to Samuel &c.; and from—אחז את הע׳, see אָחַז.

—2) anything resembling the eye, hole, ring &c. Kelim VIII, 7 ע׳ של תנור the ‘eye’ of an oven (the fire-place under the oven, Maimonides; the opening for the escape of the smoke, which may be closed to retain the heat, Rabbenu Shimshon). Ib. IX, 8 תנור שניקב מעינו an oven in the eye of which is a defect. Ib. XXI, 2 ע׳ the ring-shaped pad around an animal’s neck (a halter of soft material). Ib. ע׳ של מתכת a metal hame (compare עוֹנָתָא). Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra I, 7 העיין שבמצעד the ring attached to an adze; and from

—3) spring, well. Ketubot I, 10; and from—[Frequ. עֵין in proper noun of a place, as ע׳ סוכר, ע׳ טב; see respective determinants].

צוּמִּים, צוּמָּם m. (צָמַם, subaudi אזנים) [tied up,] a person whose auricles are a shapeless mass (instead of being carved out). Tosefta Bekhoroth IV, 15 צומים, explained ib. 16 צ׳ שאזניו מגופפות (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) צומת שאזניה וכ׳, correct accordingly שאזניו), see גָּפַף; Bekhoroth VII, 4 (44ᵃ) צִמָּם (Bavli ed. צומם; Arukh צימם), explained שאזניו דומות לספוג whose auricles resemble a sponge. Ib. (in G’mara) צימם.

צוּמָּח m. (צָמַח) [grown over, subaudi אזנים,] a person without (or with very small) auricles. Tosefta Bekhoroth IV, 15, explained ib. 16 צ׳ כל שאין לו אזנים (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) צומוס, correct accordingly) a tsummaḥ is an animal which has no external ears; Bekhoroth VII, 4 (44ᵃ) צמע (Bavli ed. צומע, Arukh צימח), explained שאזניו קטנות. Ib. (in G’mara) צימע, and צומע.—[V. צִימֵּחַ.]

sections.en: The mishna lists additional blemishes that disqualify a priest from performing the Temple service: If a priest’s eyes are large like those of a calf or small like those of a goose; if his body is disproportionately large relative to his limbs or disproportionately small relative to his limbs; if his nose is disproportionately large relative to his limbs or disproportionately small relative to his limbs, he is disqualified. And the tzomem and the tzome’a are also disqualified. What is a tzome’a? It is anyone whose ears are small. And what is the tzomem? It is anyone whose ears are similar to a sponge.
sections.he: עֵינָיו גְּדוֹלוֹת כְּשֶׁל עֵגֶל, אוֹ קְטַנּוֹת כְּשֶׁל אַוָּז, גּוּפוֹ גָּדוֹל מֵאֵבָרָיו אוֹ קָטָן מֵאֵבָרָיו, חָטְמוֹ גָּדוֹל מֵאֵבָרָיו אוֹ קָטָן מֵאֵבָרָיו, הַצִּמֵּם, וְהַצִּמֵּעַ. אֵיזֶה הוּא צִמֵּעַ, שֶׁאָזְנָיו קְטַנּוֹת. וְהַצִּמֵּם, שֶׁאָזְנָיו דּוֹמוֹת לִסְפוֹג:

en: אֶשֶׁךְ m. (Biblical Hebrew; denominative of אִישׁ) testicle. plural אֲשָׁכִים. Bekhoroth VII, 5 (44ᵇ). Tosefta ib. V, 4.—Denom. מְאוּשְׁכָּן one having large testicles. Bekhoroth l. common gender. (Ib. ed. מאושבן, see שעבז).

גֶּבֶר m. (Biblical Hebrew; גבר)
1) man, master. Eicha Rabbah to III, 1. Kiddushin 80ᵇ (reference. to Eicha III, 39) וכי ג׳ על הטאיו הוא (Rashi) is man master over his sins (sinless)?

—2) cock. Yoma I, 8 בקריאת הג׳ at the time of the crowing of the cock; ib. 20ᵇ; Yerushalmi Shekalim V, 48ᵈ bottom of page; Yerushalmi Sukkah V, 55ᶜ disputed meaning: man’s (the cryer’s) crying, or the cock’s crowing, see כָּרוֹזָא.

—3) (euphem.) membrum virile. Bekhoroth VII, 5 (44ᵇ) בעל ג׳ a man with an abnormally large membrum.

חָשׁוּךְ m. (Biblical Hebrew; חָשַׁךְ)
1) dark, black. Pirkei Avot Zar. 8ᵃ, see חָשַׁךְ.—plural חֲשׁוּכִּים, כִּין …; f. חֲשׁוּכּוֹת. Bekhoroth VII, 5 (explained מרוח אשך, Vayikra XXI, 20) שמראיו ח׳ whose complexion is very dark. Yalkut Shemot 258 פנים ח׳ dark (frowning) countenance; Mekhilta Beshalach, Vayassa, section (Parashah) 2 חֲשֵׁכוֹת.

—2) obscured, benighted. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 6, beginning (reference. to Mishlei XXII, 29) פרעה הח׳ Pharaoh, the benighted.—plural as ab. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to I, 1 (reference. to Mishlei l. common gender.) לפני ח׳ אלו הרשעים ‘before the benighted’ that means the wicked.

מְרוֹחַ m. (Biblical Hebrew; see מָרַח)
1) (denominative of רוח) filled with air. Bekhoroth VII, 5 (explained Vayikra XXI, 20) כל שרוח וכ׳ he who has wind in his testicles; Tosefta ib. V, 4 (see קילֵיטֵיס); Yalkut Vayikra 632.

—2) (= מְמוֹרָח, see מָרַח) smashed. Ib. (R. Yishm.) שנמרחו וכ׳; (Tosefta l. common gender. שחוף).—[
3) מ׳ אשך = מַרְאֵה חשֶׁךְ black complexion. Bekhoroth l. common gender., opinion of R. Antigonos.]

מַרְאֶה , m.(b. h.; sight, looks, appearance; color, shade. Yoma 74ᵇ מַרְאֵה עינים באשה the pleasure of looking at one’s wife. Tosefta Negaim I, 2 מ׳ ראשון the first inspection of a leprous affection (Vayikra XIII, 3), מ׳ שני the second (ib. 5) &c. Ib. 4 כל מ׳ לבן all shades of white; מ׳ סיבות grey color. Ib. 5 מ׳ גבוה the appearance of an elevation; כמ׳ צל בחמה as the appearance of a shade thrown on a sunlit object; Sifra Thazr., Negaim, Chaldaic I; and from—plural מַרְאוֹת (with pronom. suffix) מַרְאָיו, מַרְאֶיהָ &c. Negaim I, 1. Sifra l. common gender., Parah 2, Chaldaic II במראיו its retaining original color; כהה ממראיו fainter than its original color. Bekhoroth VII, 5; see חָשׁוּךְ; and from

מָרַח (Biblical Hebrew; sec. root or radix of רוח) to soften; to poultice.

Piël - מֵירֵחַ
1) to strike a plaster, rub a salve; in gen. to mash, crush. Tosefta Shabbat V (VI), 6 המְמָרֵחַ בשבת he who mashes ingredients for a plaster on the Sabbath; Eruvin 102ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. X, 26ᶜ.—Shabbat 75ᵇ הממ׳ רטיה וכ׳ he who spreads and presses the poultice over a sore; Yerushalmi ib. VII, 10ᵈ top. Ib. XXII, 3 (146ᵃ) he must not put on wax מפני שהוא ממרח (Mishnah Pesachim מַמְרִיחַ, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 90) because it is an act resembling the spreading of plaster. Sifra Sh’mini, Parah 8, Chaldaic X; Kelim V, 11 מֵרְחָהּ בטיט if he smeared clay over it; Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma IV, 10; 12. Ib. VII, 10 ומי׳ שפתותיה עם הכותל and connected its rims with the wall by plaster or pitch; and from—Part. pass. מְמוֹרָח crushed. Bekhoroth 44ᵇ האי ממ׳ אשך וכ׳ (not ממרוח) if m’roaḥ meant crushed, it ought to read m’moraḥ &c.; Yalkut Vayikra 632, see מְרוֹחַ.

—2) to pass (the hand) over a viscid mass, to wipe off, rub off. Yerushalmi Shabbat VII, 10ᵃ bottom of page מְמָרְחוֹ בידו אחת he may wipe (or brush) it off with one hand; (Bavli ib. 141ᵃ מגרר בצפרן).

—3) to give a pile of grain an even shape, to finish the process of storing up. Ma'asrot I, 6 משיְמָרֵחַ ואם אינו מְמָרֵחַ וכ׳ (Yerushalmi ed. מְמָרֵיחַ or מַמְרִיחַ) (is subject to tithes) as soon as he evens the pile, and if he does not even &c.; explained Yerushalmi ib. I, 49ᵃ bottom of page מן דו ישפר וכ׳ when he gives a finish to the surface of the pile. Ib. בשאין בדעתו למָרֵחַ (not לימרח) when he has not the intention to even the pile; and from—Part. pass. מְמוֹרָח, f. מְמוֹרַחַת; plural מְמוֹרָחִין; מְמוֹרָחוֹת. Bekhoroth 11ᵃ, sq. טבלים ממ׳ (Arukh מְרוּחִים) untithed grain stored up in proper shape. Yerushalmi Peah IV, 16ᶜ bottom of page כרי ממ׳ a finished pile; and e.—Tosefta Terumot IV, 15 מוּרַחַת = ממורחת.

—4) (denominative of רַחַת) to winnow. Part. pass. as ab. Tosefta Ma'asrot II, 17 מצא תבואה ממ׳ עשויה כרי וכ׳ if one finds winnowed grain (which has been abandoned), if it is made up into a pile, you dare not take it, opposed מפוזרת scattered; Yerushalmi ib. III, 50ᶜ bottom of page פירות ממורחין.

Nifal - נִמְרַח
1) to be crushed into a viscid mass. Bekhoroth VII, 5 (explained מרוח אשך, Vayikra XXI, 20) כל שנִמְרְחוּ אשכיו (Bavli ed., 44ᵇ, נימחו) whose testicles are crushed; (refuted ib. in Ib.) האי ממורח וכ׳, see supra.

—2) to be smeared over. Tosefta Kelim Bava Kamma VII, 10 עד שתִּמָּרֵחַ עם השפה until it is smeared over so as to be even with the rim.

Hithpaël - הִתְמָרֵחַ,

Nithpaël - נִתְמָרֵחַ to be shaped into an even pile, to be finished. Yerushalmi Peah I, beginning 15ᵃ עד שלא נתמ׳ הכר as long as the pile is not struck off; and e. [Y. Ma'asrot I, 49ᵃ bottom of page תבואה משיתמרח, read: משימרח, see supra.]

נָאלָא II, נָאלָה m. (לְאִי, לְהִי, see Payne Smith, Thesaurus Syriacus 2260)
1) fatigue, heavy load; compare אוּבְצָנָא. Targum Yonatan Devarim XXI, 3 דלא סליק בנ׳ שעבוד דניר Arukh, read: דלא סליק עלה דכר ולא אטרחא בנ׳ (שעבוד דניר being a gloss interpreting נאלא); compare Targum Yonatan Bamidbar XIX, 2.

—2) incubus, asthma believed to be caused by a demon בן נפלים. Bekhoroth 44ᵇ (reference. to רוח קצרה or קצרית, Mishnah ib. VII, 5) מאי ניהו נאלה Arukh (Rashi נאלת or נאלח, read נאלה; missing in Talmud ed.) what is it? Nâla. [Prob. version: מאי ניהו נ׳ מאי נ׳ תנא רוח בן נפלים וכ׳.]

קַצְרוּת, קַצְרִית f. (preceding) רוח ק׳ asthma, or incubus [or nervous prostration,] believed to be caused by a demon, Ben N’filim. Bekhoroth VII, 5 (44ᵇ) רוח קצרית באה עליו Mishnah (Bavli ed. קצרה) a person subject to asthmatic spells (is unfit for priesthood). Ib. 44ᵇ רוח קצרות, see נָאלָא II and נָפִיל.

שִׁעְבֵּז (see next word), participle pass. מְשׁוּעְבָּז one who has abnormally large testicles or an abnormally long scrotum. Bekhoroth VII, 5 (44ᵇ) Arukh (Mishnah ed. מאושכן, Talmud ed. מאושבן), see אֶשֶׁךְ.

שָׁחַף (see חָפַף II) to rub, scrape, peel. —Part. pass. שָׁחוּף a) one whose genitals are wasted (see מָחוּי). Tosefta Bekhoroth V, 4 (explained מרוח אשך, for which Bekhoroth VII, 5 שנמרחו אשכיו, see מָרַח). Sotah 26ᵇ. Esther Rabbah to II, 3.—b) (compare חֲסִיךְ) reduced, lean, losing flesh. Sifra Bechukotai, Parah 2, Chaldaic IV (reference. to שחפת, Vayikra XXVI, 16) או עתים שהוא ש׳ וכ׳ or at times one becomes reduced in flesh, but feels comfortable &c.; Yalkut Vayikra 673 נשחוף (correct accordingly).—Yalkut Breishit 146 שְׁחוּפִים, see סָכַף.—*c) f. שְׁחוּפָה; plural שְׁחוּפוֹת of indistinct color, gray (wool), opposed לבנות. Chullin XI, 2 (135ᵃ; ib. 136ᵇ (Manuscript Rome 2 סחופות; Manuscript Rome 1, and Arukh טחופות, see טָחַף).

Nifal - נִשְׁחָף to become reduced. Sifra l. common gender. (reference. to שחפת, see supra) יש לך אדם … שהוא נ׳ (not וכי יש) sometimes a person is sick in bed, yet his flesh is preserved: therefore the text says, ‘and consumption’, which means that he is wasting away; Yalkut Vayikra l. common gender.

comments.en: 15) "garav": a scabby condition. "yalefeth": the Egyptian lichen, "meroach ashech": R. Yishmael says: one whose testicles are crushed. R. Akiva says: one with distended testicles. Chanania b. Antignos says: one whose skin has taken on a swarthy coloration.
comments.he: [טו] "גרב" – זו החרס. "ילפת" – זו חזזית מצרית. "מרוח אשך" – ר' ישמעאל אומר כל שנמרחו אשכיו. ר' עקיבא אומר כל שרוח באשכיו. חנניא בן אנטיגנוס אומר כל שמראיו חשוכים.

en: The mishna teaches that one who is afflicted with a melancholy temper is disqualified from performing the Temple service. The Gemara asks: What is this melancholy temper? A tanna taught: A fallen spirit, i.e., the spirit of a demon, has come upon him.

The mishna also teaches that one whose scrotum is unnaturally long [me’ushban] and one whose penis is unnaturally long [ba’al gever] are disqualified from performing the Temple service. The Sages taught in a baraita: A meshuban is one with exceedingly large testicles, and a ba’al gever is one with an unnaturally long penis. Similarly, it is taught in a baraita: A meshuban, this is synonymous with the kayyan. The garbetan, this is synonymous with a ba’al kik. A kayyan is one with a condition of the testicles, while a garbeta is one with a condition of the penis.

The Gemara asks: And how much is considered too long, which disqualifies the priest from performing the Temple service? Rav Yehuda pointed and said: Until the knee. It is likewise taught in a baraita that Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says: If one’s penis reaches until his knee he is disqualified from performing the Temple service. But if it reaches until just above his knee he remains fit. Some say if his penis reaches until the knee he is fit, but if it passes below the knee he is disqualified.

comments.en: MISHNA: If one has no testicles, or if he has only one testicle, that is the mero’aḥ ashekh that is stated in the Torah (see Leviticus 21:20) among the blemishes that disqualify a priest from Temple service. Rabbi Yishmael says: A mero’aḥ ashekh is anyone whose testicles were crushed. Rabbi Akiva says: It is anyone that has wind in his testicles, i.e., they are swollen. Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says: Mero’aḥ ashekh does not refer to the testicles; rather, the reference is to anyone whose appearance [marav] is especially dark [ḥashukhin].
comments.he: מתני׳ אין לו ביצים או אין לו אלא ביצה אחת הרי זה (ויקרא כא, כ) מרוח אשך האמור בתורה רבי ישמעאל אומר כל שנימוחו אשכיו ר"ע אומר כל שרוח באשכיו רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס אומר כל שמראיו חשוכין:

comments.en: The firstborn animal may be slaughtered if it has no testicles or if it has only one testicle. Rabbi Yishmael says: If the animal has two scrotal sacs, it can be assumed that it has two testicles; if the animal does not have two scrotal sacs, it can be assumed that it has only one testicle. Rabbi Akiva says: The matter can be ascertained: One seats the animal on its rump and mashes the sac; if there is a testicle, ultimately it is going to emerge. There was an incident where one mashed the sac and the testicle did not emerge. Then, the animal was slaughtered and the testicle was discovered attached to the loins. And Rabbi Akiva permitted the consumption of its flesh, as the testicle had not previously emerged, and Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri prohibited its consumption.
comments.he: אֵין לוֹ בֵיצִים, (אוֹ) אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵּיצָה אֶחָת. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, אִם יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁנֵי כִיסִין, יֵשׁ לוֹ שְׁתֵּי בֵיצִים. אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא כִיס אֶחָד, אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵיצָה אֶחָת. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, מוֹשִׁיבוֹ עַל עַכּוּזוֹ וּמְמַעֵךְ, אִם יֵשׁ שָׁם בֵּיצָה, סוֹפָהּ לָצֵאת. מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁמִּעֵךְ וְלֹא יָצָאת, וְנִשְׁחַט וְנִמְצֵאת דְּבוּקָה בַּכְּסָלִים, וְהִתִּיר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא וְאָסַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי:

comments.en: When a firstborn had only one testicle, but two sacs, it was sat on its rear, and its genital area kneaded without finding the second testicle, an expert granted permission for its slaughter and it was slaughtered, it is permitted to be eaten even though the second testicle was found clinging to the flanks. Since its genital area was kneaded, the original ruling is not rescinded. If, however, its genital area was not kneaded, even though permission to slaughter it was granted by an expert, it must be buried.
comments.he: בְּכוֹר שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ בֵּיצָה אַחַת וּשְׁנֵי כִּיסִים. וּבְדָקוֹ הַמֻּמְחֶה וְהוֹשִׁיבוּהוּ עַל הַרְגּוֹזוֹ וּמִעֲכוּ וְלֹא יָצָאת בֵּיצָה שְׁנִיָּה וְהִתִּירוֹ הַמֻּמְחֶה וְנִשְׁחַט וְנִמְצָא הַשְּׁנִיָּה דְּבוּקָה בַּכְּסָלִים הֲרֵי זֶה מֻתָּר הוֹאִיל וּמִעֲכוּ. אֲבָל אִם לֹא נִמְעַךְ אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנִּשְׁחַט עַל פִּי מֻמְחֶה הֲרֵי זֶה יִקָּבֵר:
אין לו ביצים או אין לו אלא ביצה אחת - הוי מום:
שני כיסין - לכל בהמה יש לה לכל ביצה כיס אחת לפי שהכיס חלוק באמצעיתו ומבחוץ ניכר שהרי באמצע הוא משוקע ונראית בו שורה העמוקה:
ומושיבין אותו על עכוזו - גרסינן. והכי אמרינן בעירובין בפ' כיצד מעברין (עירובין דף נג:) אכוזו תנן או עכוזו תנן. על עכוזו על עגבותיו אחת מושיבין את הבכור שאין לו אלא ביצה אחת:
וממעך - וממשמש בכיס ובכסלים ואם יש סופה לצאת ואם אינה יוצאה הוי מום:
כסלים - פלנק"ש:
והתיר ר"ע - דהוי מום הואיל ואינה במקומה:
עכוזו [אינטער לייב] (בכורות מ) מושיבו על עכוזו וממעך פי' בל' יוני כוזו עגבות (ע' ערך הרגוזו):

א משנה ועוד מומים ששוחטים עליהם את הבכור מחוץ למקדש: אין לו ביצים (אשכים), או אין לו אלא ביצה אחת. ר' ישמעאל אומר: אם יש לו שני כיסין של ביצים — יש לו שתי ביצים, אין לו שני כיסין, אלא אחד — אין לו אלא ביצה אחת. ר' עקיבא אומר: ניתן לברר את הדבר. כיצד? מושיבו על עכוזו (אחוריו) וממעך, ממשמש ודוחק באותו מקום, לפי שאם יש ביצה — סופו לצאת. ואם מיעך ולא יצאה — הרי זה מום, ומותר לשחוט את הבכור. מסופר, מעשה בבכור שלא היתה לו אלא ביצה אחת, שמיעך ולא יצא ביצה שניה, ונשחטה הבהמה, כדין בכור בעל מום, ונמצאת הביצה דבוקה בכסלים (בחלק הפנימי של הירך), והתיר ר' עקיבא לאכול את בשר הבכור, מפני שלא יצאה על ידי מיעוך, ואסר ר' יוחנן בן נורי.

comments.he: מתני׳ אין לו ביצים או אין לו אלא ביצה אחת ר' ישמעאל אומר אם יש לו שני כיסין יש לו ב' ביצים אין לו שני כיסין אין לו אלא ביצה אחת ר"ע אומר מושיבו על עכוזו וממעך אם יש ביצה סופו לצאת מעשה שמיעך ולא יצא נשחטה ונמצאת דבוקה בכסלים והתיר ר"ע ואסר רבי יוחנן בן נורי:

en: GEMARA: The Gemara asks: What is the ruling taught in the previous mishna that the tanna is referring to when he teaches here: And there was an incident? The Gemara answers: Since we learned in the list of blemishes in the previous mishna the case where its mouth is similar to that of a pig, and the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Ila in that case, we say here that when the Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Ila, it is only in a case where its upper lip overlaps the lower lip. But in a case where the lower jaw protrudes beyond the upper jaw, everyone agrees that this is a blemish.

The Gemara continues this version of the mishna: And there was also an incident where the lower jaw of the firstborn protruded beyond the upper jaw, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel asked the Sages for a ruling, and they said: That is a blemish that enables the slaughter of the firstborn.

The Gemara challenges: But it is with regard to the blemishes of a person that we learned in a mishna (44a): If his upper lip protrudes beyond the lower lip or his lower lip protrudes beyond the upper lip, that is a blemish. And it is only with regard to a person that it is written: “Whatever man of the seed of Aaron” (Leviticus 22:4), which teaches that in order to be fit for the Temple service a priest must be a man who is equal to the seed of Aaron, i.e., he has an ordinary appearance like other priests. But this requirement is not stated with regard to an animal, and therefore an animal should not be considered blemished if its lower lip protrudes beyond the upper lip.

Rav Pappa said in response: That is not difficult; this mishna is referring to a case where the lower jaw contains a bone that is longer than the upper jaw, in which case it is a blemish even for an animal, whereas that mishna is referring to a case where the lower jaw does not contain a bone, and therefore it is a blemish only in the case of a person.

sections.en: If his upper lip protrudes beyond the lower lip or his lower lip protrudes beyond the upper lip, that is a blemish. And one whose teeth fell out is disqualified due to the appearance of a blemish. The mishna lists additional blemishes that disqualify a priest from performing the Temple service: One who has breasts so large that they sag like those of a woman; or if one’s belly is swollen and protrudes; or if one’s navel protrudes; or if one is an epileptic, even if he experiences seizures only once in a long while; or one who is afflicted with a melancholy temper; or one whose scrotum is unnaturally long; or one whose penis is unnaturally long is disqualified from performing the Temple service. If one has no testicles, or if he has only one testicle, that is the mero’aḥ ashekh that is stated in the Torah (see Leviticus 21:20) among the blemishes that disqualify a priest from Temple service. Rabbi Yishmael says: A mero’aḥ ashekh is anyone whose testicles were crushed. Rabbi Akiva says: It is anyone that has wind in his testicles, i.e., they are swollen. Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus says: Mero’aḥ ashekh does not refer to the testicles; rather, the reference is to anyone whose appearance [marav] is especially dark [ḥashukhin].
sections.he: שְׂפָתוֹ הָעֶלְיוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנָה, וְהַתַּחְתּוֹנָה עוֹדֶפֶת עַל הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, הֲרֵי זֶה מוּם. וְשֶׁנִּטְּלוּ שִׁנָּיו, פָּסוּל, מִפְּנֵי מַרְאִית הָעָיִן. דַּדָּיו שׁוֹכְבִים כְּשֶׁל אִשָּׁה, כְּרֵסוֹ צָבָה, טַבּוּרוֹ יוֹצֵא, נִכְפֶּה אֲפִלּוּ אַחַת לְיָמִים, רוּחַ קַצְרִית בָּאָה עָלָיו, הַמְאֻשְׁכָּן, וּבַעַל גֶּבֶר. אֵין לוֹ בֵיצִים, אוֹ אֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא בֵיצָה אַחַת, זֶהוּ מְרוֹחַ אָשֶׁךְ הָאָמוּר בַּתּוֹרָה. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר, כּל שֶׁנִּמְרְחוּ אֲשָׁכָיו. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר, כּל שֶׁרוּחַ בַּאֲשָׁכָיו. רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס אוֹמֵר, כֹּל שֶׁמַּרְאָיו חֲשׁוּכִין:

en: *הִדְרָנִיקוֹס m. (a corruption of ὑδερικός or ὑδρωπικός, compare הִדְרוֹקָן; for Variant lect. see infra) one afflicted with dropsy. Berakhot 58ᵇ ואת הננס ואת ה׳ (Manuscript Munich ואת הרדינקס, Manuscript Florence והננס ה׳); Tosefta ib. VII (VI), 3 (absent in ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta), added in note); Midrash Tanḥuma Pinḥ. 10 … הבהקנין ואת דרניקוס; ed. Bub. ib. 1 ואת הדרקונוס … הננס (Mss. הדריקינוס, הדרקוניס); Yerushalmi Berakhot IX, 13ᵇ bottom of page (absent); [absent in Bekhoroth VII, 6, among bodily blemishes disqualifying for priestly service]. [Our word is obviously a gloss to one of the anomalies enumerated in the text, probably to קִפֵּחַ.—Arukh reads והברדניקוס, in the place of קפח in our text, giving it the meaning of כִּיפֵּחַ see as well, but records also הדר׳ in letter He; Hilkhot Rabbeinu Alfasi reads בדריקנוס, בדרקינוס, leaving out קפח.—For other definitions of our word, see commentaries.]
גִּיחוֹר m. (see גִּיהַּ and גִּיהְיָא)red-spotted in the face. Bekhoroth VII, 6, explained ib. 45ᵇ סומקא. Berakhot 58ᵇ; and e.

דִּלְדּוּל, דִּיל׳ m. (see next word)
1) a limb torn in shreds, strips &c. Chullin 46ᵃ די׳ זה וכ׳ as to this case of (נדלדלה) the liver found to be torn &c.

—2) wart with a thin neck, see יַבֶּלֶת. plural דִּלְדּוּלִין, דִּי׳. Negaim VI, 7 (Tosefta ib. II, 2 תלתלין); Sifra Thazr., Negaim, Parah 1, Chaldaic II. Bekhoroth VII, 6 (45ᵇ, Rashi תלתולין) בעלי הד׳ persons or animals afflicted with large warts. Negaim VI, 8 הד׳ שבראש וכ׳ (hairless) warts on the head or chin (Tos’f. Yom Tob: isolated hair-grown spots).

יָתֵר, יָתֵיר m. (preceding wds.)
1) additional, a person having an additional limb. Bekhoroth VII, 6 י׳ בידיו וכ׳ if one has an additional finger (or toe) on each of his hands and feet. Ib. 45ᵇ.—Ib. 40ᵃ חסר וי׳ ביד having one toe less or one too many on the forefoot. Ib. כל יתיר כנטול דמי every addition is considered equal to the entire absence of the respective limb; Chullin 58ᵇ כל יתר וכ׳. Bava Batra VII, 2, sq. הן י׳ (יתיר and יתר interchanging), see הֵן; and from—Fem. יְתֵרָה, יְתֵירָה; (as noun also) יְתֶרֶת, יְתֶירֶת. Bekhoroth VII, 6 (45ᵃ) היתה (בה) בו יתרת וכ׳ (Rashi יתירה; Ib. יתירת) if there has been an additional limb and he had it cut off. Ib. 40ᵃ י׳ על של משה וכ׳ (a cubit measure) larger than the Mosaic by &c. Chullin III, 6 (as a sign of clean birds) כל שיש לו אצבע י׳ that which has an additional toe (on top of those in a line). Ketubot 76ᵃ יתירת a woman having an additional limb. Eruvin 83ᵃ י׳ על מדברית וכ׳ one sixth larger than &c.; and from [V. יְתֵירָה.]—plural יְתֵרִים, יְתֵרִין, יְתֵי׳; f. יְתֵירוֹת. Makkot 23ᵃ יְתֵירֵי מדע men of more than ordinary knowledge; י׳ כח of more than common physical strength.—[Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 98 הניחו יתירות left remants of the conquered nations, probably to be read: יְתֵידוֹת, see יָתֵד.]—Esp. יְתֶרֶת an additional lobe of the lungs. Chullin 47ᵃ (not יות׳).

—2) a word written plene, with vowel letters.—plural יְתֵירוֹת. Eruvin 13ᵃ, and e., see חָסֵר II.

כִּיפֵּחַ, (כִּיפֵּיחַ), קִיפֵּ׳, קִפֵּ׳ m. (כָּפַח, קָפַח, see כּוּפָּח)
1) (subaudi שוקים) one having high and arched shoulders, hump-backed. Yerushalmi Ketubot VII, end, 31ᵈ עובדא … בכ׳ (not בכופיח) a case (petition for divorce) came before R. J. against a husband who had become hump-backed (after marriage), and he forced him (to a divorce).

—2) (see גִּבֵּחַ, גְּבִיחַ)an extremely tall and unshapely person. Bekhoroth VII, 6 (45ᵇ) כ׳ Arukh (ed. קפ׳), see גִּבֵּחַ. Yerushalmi Berakhot IX, 13ᵇ bottom of page כ׳; Bavli Berakhot 58ᵇ קפח ed. (Manuscript Munich קי׳; Manuscript Florence כופה, correct accordingly); Tosefta ib. VII (VI), 3 כ׳ (Variant כִּיפֵּיחַ, קפח); Midrash Tanḥuma Pinḥ. 10; ed. Bub. 1 ק׳. V. הִדְרָנִיקוֹס.

כּוּשִׁי, כּוּשִׁית f. (Biblical Hebrew; כּוּשׁ II) Cushite, negro; Aethiopian. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 60, beginning; Shir HaShirim Rabbah to II, 8 (not כותי), see בַּרְבָּרִי. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 73, end; and from [Bava Kamma 113ᵇ, and e. in later ed. כושי for גּוֹי or נָכְרִי.]—Sukkah III, 6 אתרוג הכ׳, explained ib. 36ᵃ דומה לכ׳ a Palestinean Ethrog resembling an Aethiopian one; (oth. opinion) a real importation from Aethiopia. Yerushalmi ib. 53ᵈ אתרוג הכ׳ פסול the Aeth. Ethrog is ritually unfit; הבא מן הכ׳ כשר one of Palestinean growth descended from an Aethiopian Ethrog is available for ritualistic use.—Transferred abnormally dark-complexioned. Bekhoroth VII, 6. Berakhot 58ᵇ; Tosefta ib. VII (VI), 3; and e.—עֵין כּוּשִׁי proper noun of a place En Kushi. Pirkei Avot Zar. 31ᵃ; Yerushalmi ib. V, 44ᵈ ע׳ כושי׳; Yerushalmi Sheviit V, 36ᵃ top ע׳ כּוּשִׁין.

לַוְקָן, לַוְו׳, לַבְ׳ m. (a denominative of λεύκη, a kind of elephantiasis) one who is white-spotted in the face. Bekhoroth VII, 6 לב׳ ed. (Rashi לוו׳); ib. 45ᵇ explained חיורא (from analogy with לוקיאני, see preceding); Tosefta ib. V, 9 לויקן (read לוו׳). Tosefta Berakhot VII (VI), 3 לווקן ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant לוקין); Yerushalmi ib. IX, 13ᵇ bottom of page לוו׳; Sifra Emor, Parah 3, Chaldaic III לב׳; Berakhot 58ᵇ לוו׳ (Manuscript Munich לוד׳, correct accordingly).

נַנָּס m. (νᾶνος, nanus, of Semitic origin, from נסס, compare ממל from מלל) dwarf; (adjective) puny, stumped. Niddah 24ᵇ, opposed אָרוּךְ; Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 9. Berakhot 58ᵇ נ׳ one whose limbs are too small for his body, opposed כִּיפֵּחַ; Tosefta ib. VII (VI), 3 ננוס ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant ננס); Yerushalmi ib. IX, 13ᵇ bottom of page; Midrash Tanḥuma ed. Bub., Pinḥas 1. Sifra Emor, Parah 3, Chaldaic III; Bekhoroth VII, 6 (45ᵇ, of animals and of men). Shir HaShirim Rabbah to II, 15; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 65 נ׳ שבננסים a puny dwarf. Midrash Till. to Psalms CXXXVII; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 31 הנ׳ הזה that dwarf (Nebuchadnezzar); and from—Chullin 63ᵃ וסימנך ננוס פסול and thy sign (to remember that the small species of שקיטנא is unclean) be, ‘the dwarf is unfit’ (for priesthood).—plural נַנָּסִים, נַנָּסִין. Shir HaShirim Rabbah l. common gender.; Breishit Rabbah l. common gender., see supra. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 37; Yalkut ib. 62 כפתורים נ׳ Caphtorites (Breishit X, 14) are dwarfs; and from—Tamid III, 5; Middot III, 5 עמודים .נ׳ small columns. Ib. V, 2 הנ׳ (subaudi עמודים).—Fem. נַנֶּסֶת. Bekhoroth 45ᵇ. Parah II, 2; and e.

נָקַף I (Biblical Hebrew; compare נגף) to bring in close contact; to knock, strike against, wound. Chullin 7ᵇ אין אדם נוֹקֵף וכ׳ no one on earth bruises his finger, unless it is decreed &c. Berakhot 7ᵇ; Megillah 6ᵇ מי שלבו נוֹקְפוֹ he whom his heart smites (who has no clear conscience). Niddah 3ᵇ, and e. לבו נוקפו ופורש he may have scruples and separate himself entirely from his wife. Midrash Till. to Psalms IX, see נֶקֶף.—Ma'aser Sheni V, 15; Sotah IX, 10 הנוֹקְפִים those who knocked the sacrifices on their heads; explained ib. 48ᵃ; Yerushalmi ib. IX, 24ᵃ bottom of page—Part. pass. נָקוּף; f. נְקוּפָה; plural נְקוּפִים, נְקוּפִין; נְקוּפוֹת. Tosefta Chullin III, 24 ביצים נ׳ לקערה eggs cracked open into a dish (Chullin 64ᵃ טרופות).

Hifil - הִנְקִיף, הִקִּיף
1) to cause a knocking together. Sotah 22ᵇ (explained נקפי) המַנְקִיף את רגליו he who knocks his feet against each other (by his mincing walk; Rashi: who causes his feet to strike against objects on the road); compare נָקַשׁ.

—2) to bring closely together. Bekhoroth VII, 6 שמַקִּיף, see נָקַשׁ. Niddah X, 7 ומַקֶּפֶת and brings the vessel which contains the Ḥallah near the dough; T’bul Yom IV, 3, sq. Beitzah IV, 5 ואין מַקִּיפִין שתי וכ׳ and you must not move two wine vessels together to put upon them &c.—Esp. (ritual law, in examining an organic defect found in a slaughtered animal) to create a defect similar and near to the one found, in order to ascertain whether the latter was not the result of an accident after slaughtering; in gen. to compare. Chullin 50ᵃ מַקִּיפִים בבני מעים we may compare defects in entrails in which was found a perforation the origin of which is doubtful by making a hole next to it. Ib. מקיפין בקנה we may compare defects in windpipes; and from—Kiddushin 40ᵃ אין מקיפין בחילול השם no comparing (balancing of sins against good deeds) is granted when the Name of God is profaned; (oth. interpret., see נָקַף II).—Part. pass. מוּקָּף brought near. Eruvin 30ᵇ; Chullin 7ᵃ; and from לתרום שלא מן המ׳ to take T’rumah out of a mass which is not in close neighborhood of those products which are to be redeemed; Bikkurim II, 5; Terumot IV, 3; and e.

נָקַשׁ (see קִשְׁקַשׁ I) to strike against; to touch closely. Bekhoroth VII, 6 (45ᵃ) (explained עיקל) כל שמקיף … נוֹקְשׁוֹת וכ׳ (Mishnah ed. נושקות) he whose legs do not touch each other when he puts his feet together. Megillah 12ᵇ, see infra.

Hifil - הִקִּישׁ
1) to cause striking against; to knock. Bekhoroth l. common gender. (44ᵇ) המַקִּישׁ בקרסוליו וכ׳ he who knocks his ankle-bones against each other (in walking, because his legs are bent outward), or rubs his legs against each other (his feet being bent outward). Midrash Samuel Chaldaic IX מַקֶּשֶׁת ברגליה ומקשת בקרניה she knocks (creates a loud sound) with her feet and with her horns. Zavim IV, 1, sq. ה׳ על וכ׳ if he knocked against &c. Megillah 12ᵇ (play on בן קיש, Esther II, 5) שה׳ על וכ׳ (Manuscript Munich שנָקַשׁ) he (Mordecai) knocked at the gates of mercy &c.; and from—Esp. (compare נָגַן, נָכָה) to strike an instrument, play. Tamid VII, 3. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 18 (play on הפעם, Breishit II, 23) עתידה להַקִּישׁ עלי כזוג (‘Rashi’: לקשקש) she is destined to be loud against me like a bell. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 31; Midrash Till. to Psalms CXXXVII אני מבקש שתעמדו ותַקִּישׁוּ … כדרך שהייתם מַקִּישִׁין וכ׳ I desire that you play on the cithern before me and the idol, as you played before your God. Ib. אנו עומדים להַקִּישׁ וכ׳ shall we stand playing before this dwarf (Nebuchadnezzar) and this idol? Midrash Till. to Psalms XCII, end (play on יקשן, Breishit XXV, 2) שהיו מקישין בתוף לעכו"ם they struck the timbrel before idols; Yalkut Chr. 1073; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 61 מקשין בית׳
(correct accordingly).—2) (compare נָקַף) to bring under the same category by juxtaposition, to compare. Kiddushin 5ᵃ, and from (reference. to ויצאה and והיתה in the same verse, Devarim XXIV, 2) מקיש הויה ליציאה, see הֲוָיָה. Sanhedrin 60ᵇ (reference. to Shemot XXII, 19 and XXXIV, 14) זביחה בכלל … להַקִּישׁ אליה slaughtering for the idol would have been included in worshipping, and why is it singled out? To compare all other idolatrous functions with it: as slaughtering is a function performed inside &c. Zevachim 5ᵇ הִקִּישׁוֹ הכתוב וכ׳ the text (Vayikra VII, 37) places it side by side with peace offerings; and from

Hof. - הוּקַּשׁ to be placed side by side, to be compared. Keritot 3ᵃ (reference. to Bamidbar XV, 29, sq.) הוּקְּשָׁה כל התורה וכ׳ all the laws of the Torah are here placed on an equality with idolatry (as regards conditions of punishment). Ib. 2ᵇ הוּקְּשׁוּ כל העריות כולן וכ׳ all laws concerning incest are put on an equality with &c. (Vayikra XVIII, 29); and from—Part. מוּקָּשׁ. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 35 (play on קשתי, Breishit IX, 13) דבר שהוא מ׳ לי something comparable with me (with the Divine Glory); Yalkut ib. 61; see קִישׁוּת II.
עִיקֵּל m. (עָקַל) bandy-legged. Bekhoroth VII, 6 (45ᵃ), see נָקַשׁ; Sifra Emor, Chaldaic II, Parah 3 עִיקְלָן; Tosefta Bekhoroth V, 9 עִקְלָן.

פִּיקָא, פִּיקָה I f. (פקק; compare פְּקַעַת) lump, ball, swelling, especially
1) protruding cartilage. Chullin X, 4 (134ᵇ) פ׳ של גרגרת thyroid cartilage; Negaim X, 9. Ib. 10 פ׳ של צואר the protruding cartilage of the neck; Tosefta ib. IV, 12 פ׳ של פירקא. Bekhoroth VII, 6 (45ᵃ) פ׳ יוצאה מגודלו (not יצא) one that has a lump on his thumb; and from

—2) a protuberance on the blossom end of fruits, see פִּיטְמָא II. Yerushalmi Sukkah III, 53ᵈ פיקא.

—3) spinner’s coil. Oholot VII, 4 עד שיעגילו ראש כפ׳ until the embryos (on leaving the vagina) form a round head like a coil; explained Bekhoroth 22ᵃ כפ׳ של צמר like a coil of wool. Ib.; Tosefta Oholot VIII, 8 פ׳ של שתי the coil containing the warp; פ׳ של ערב containing the woof. Bekhoroth l. common gender. נראית פ׳ מתוך פ׳ it has the appearance of a coil coming forth out of a coil, see טְפִיפִית.

—4) (של כוש) פ׳ whorl. Kelim XI, 6. Parah XII, 8; and e.

—5) coil or tuft used as a stopper (see פָּקַק). Kelim XVII, 12.—plural פִּיקִין; פִּיקוֹת. Bekhoroth 45ᵃ בעל הפיקין (not הקיפין) one afflicted with lumps; (Arukh Variant הפיקס; Arukh section (Parashah) see כסת: הפִּיקָן; Mishnah ib. VII, 6 בעל פיקה; Talmud ed. 45ᵃ הפיקום, Rashi: הפיקין). Ib. 22ᵃ שלש פ׳ שמעתי וכ׳ I learned of three sizes of coils, one of the warp, one of the woof, and one large coil, that of the sack-weavers; Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia VII, 1, see סַקָּי I. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 14 פ׳ פ׳ coils upon coils (in the abdomen). Tosefta Oholot XIII, 5, see לָבַשׁ; and e.

קָלַט (Biblical Hebrew) [to surround,]
1) to close, press.—Part. pass. קָלוּט; f. קְלוּטָה; plural קְלוּטִים; קְלוּטיֹת. Sifra Emor, Parah 7, Chaldaic VII (explained קלוט, Vayikra XXII, 23) פרסוֹת וכ׳ an animal whose hoofs resemble those of a horse &c.; Bekhoroth VI, 7 (40ᵃ) שרגליו ק׳ וכ׳. Bekhoroth 6ᵃ פרסותיה ק׳ its hoofs are closed, opposed סדוקות cloven. Ib. VII, 6 אצבעותיו … או ק׳ וכ׳ if his fingers lie one above the other or are grown together up to the root (פֶּרֶק). Yerushalmi Sotah IX, 23ᵈ; and e.—In gen. קָלוּט an animal with uncloven hoofs (having the sign of uncleanness) born of a clean animal, monster or hybrid. Bekhoroth 7ᵃ ק׳ בן פרה a ḳaluṭ born of a cow; Chullin 68ᵇ. Ib. ק׳ במעי פרה a ḳaluṭ found in a cow (after ritual slaughtering); ib. 69ᵃ. Shabbat 67ᵃ זרעיך כק׳ וכפרדה וכ׳ thy seed be like a ḳ. and like a mule &c. (Rashi: ‘like one whose semen is locked up’); and e.

—2) to clutch, intercept, receive; to conceive, retain, absorb. Chullin 65ᵃ כל עוף הקוֹלֵט מן האויר וכ׳ any bird that snatches in the air (for things thrown to it) is unclean. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 41 אינה קוֹלֶטֶת, see פֶּרֶד II. Keritot 5ᵃ וק׳ את הריח and the oil retained (absorbed) the scent. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 5 קְלָטָן הים the sea absorbed them (the waters of the rivers); Yalkut Psalms 848 קְלָטָם. Pirkei Avot V, 15 שמוציאה את היין וקולטת וכ׳ which passes the wine and retains the lees; שמוציאה … וק׳ את הסולת which passes the common flour and retains the fine flour (see צוּף). Sanhedrin 108ᵇ כל שהתיבה קוֹלַטְתּוֹ whatever animal the ark received. Shabbat I, 6 כדי שיִקְלוֹט העין when there is time enough before the Sabbath for the wool to assume the color of the dye. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 14 אין האשה קולטת וכ׳ a woman conceives only shortly after menstruation. Sheviit II, 6 כל הרכבה שאינה קולטת וכ׳ a grafting which does not take root within three days, will never do so; and see from—Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 1 ק׳ דרך וכ׳ he (Moses) adopted the manner of his ancestors (finding wives at the well); Midrash Tanḥuma Sh’moth 10 לקח.—Esp. (see מִקְלָט) to protect, give the shelter of an asylum. Makkot 12ᵃ אינו קולט אלא גגו only the top of the altar protects him that flees to it; אינו קולט … עולמים only the altar of the permanent sanctuary (in Jerusalem) offers protection; אינו קולט אלא כהן וכ׳ protects only the priest while at service &c. Ib. לא קָלְטָה אחת מהם עד וכ׳ none of those cities had the right of asylum until all of them had been designated; and from—Makkot 10ᵃ מנין … קוֹלְטִין whence do you learn that the words of the Law offer protection (to its students)?; ib. קולטין ממלאך וכ׳ they protect from the angel of death.
